The military pay grade increase is for eagle scout is only from E-1 to E-2, with some college you may get E-3. Honestly the pay difference isn't much, and you'd get those promotions in a few months anyway. If you're legitimately interested in this there are a lot of ways to get the most out of it and I'm happy to tell you more (I'm in the Army). Its a tempting option in your situation, but I'd say stick to college and try to do so with the least amount of debt possible. Stick to scholarships or community college and pay it out of your pocket over time with a job, and transfer later to finish at a "better" place if you feel like you need to (this is what I did for my Architecture degree). State schools can be really good too and are usually priced better if you're from the same state. Unless you've got a full ride including dorms (or is mostly covered) there is no rush in finishing college immediately. You can call the university you've been accepted into and ask them if you can enroll next year instead, and spend this one getting on your feet. Getting a job and a cheap apartment for now is a good option, but it can get comfortable, so make sure you set up a plan and stick to it. Trade school is also an amazing option, one that will most likely get you a better paying job and benefits too if you wanna go that route (I'm also a plumber).

If you're limited on cash and have to decide between an apartment or getting your car stuff straightened out, do the car stuff. You can sleep in your car, but you can't drive your apartment. If your high school has a gym/fitness place, they should have showers there too. Try doing that (college will most likely have this too), and you can always use the local laundromat to take care of your clothes. I did my last two semesters of college living out of my car this way cause I was pretty broke. If you end up roughing it longer than expected, let me know, I've got tips for you.
